text: FACTSTRIP HAS A THIRD SHAPE: `variant="bar"`, the brand-blue band the website home page carries under its scheme portals. No marks, the caption above the figure, a hairline between the cells, and — through the new `action` prop — a control in a cell of its own. It inverts, white type on `bg/brand/primary/bolder`, which is why it is asked for by name and never selected by item count: a set that fell into it by arithmetic would put white on blue with nobody deciding to. `action` is ignored by the other two shapes, because a strip of facts has nothing after it and a cell holding a button would borrow a fact's width. Items gain an optional `unit`: the bar sets the figure at 48px, where "₹67,977 Crore" written into `value` is 330px of type in a 270px cell and wraps, so the unit is set a size down beside the number — `headline-2` complete, weight included, so a unit is never lighter than the figure it qualifies. Everywhere else `unit` renders on the same line at the same size, so a strip that has always written the unit into `value` reads identically whichever way it supplies it. TWO GAPS RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. The bar is flat where the design draws a left-to-right gradient from #0260B8 to #0373DF: the first stop is `bg/brand/primary/bolder` to within two points, and the second is gov-blue, which no Tier-2 background token resolves to — the ramp runs 50, 100, 200, 300, 600, 800 and skips 500, and component CSS may not reach past the semantic layer to a Palette rung. And the SAMAVESH library has no `Type=Bar` variant: Figma was unreachable when this shipped, so the set, its documentation page and its Code Connect enum all owe one.
